final_rationale: The verdict changes to noncompliant, but not because of new admissible evidence. The Actor provided no new evidence and expressly relied on the same record. What changed is the interpretation of that record in light of the policy predicate. On the available evidence, the exposed insurance claims triage use case remains in scope, approved risk acceptance is absent, and completed required disclosure is not shown. Under the stated criteria, that is not merely a plausible but incompletely supported certification case; it is a failed compliance condition. The Actor's narrowed position is more disciplined than an unconditional certification claim, but caveating that certification could proceed if disclosure were completed does not satisfy a requirement that has not been shown satisfied on the present record. Monitoring and reversible rollout support operational risk control, but they do not cure the unresolved disclosure predicate.
remaining_concerns: The affected insurance claims triage use case remains in scope for the initial rollout cohort.
The segment is below target on catastrophe-claim evidence triage.
There is no approved risk acceptance covering the exposed use case.
The present record does not show completed pre-launch model-card disclosure for the named exposed use case.
Policy states rollout controls, rollback capability, and monitoring do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.
